notes: Windows revision 4. Fixes 'Runtime error (at 9:1079): Type Mismatch' on clean Windows Server 2025. Root cause: the #13#10 (CRLF char literal) string concatenation in MsgBox / Log calls in the Inno [Code] section - Inno 7.x Pascal's runtime dispatcher does not coerce Char to String in multi-term concatenation, raising ETypeMismatch at a function-specific bytecode offset. r4 removes every #13 / #10 char literal from the [Code] section; all user-facing messages are now single-line string literals (no char concatenation), and multi-line output is achieved by issuing several Log() calls instead. Post-install validation still checks the on-disk deliverables (CertMateService.exe, export_pfx.py, updater.py) via FileExists only - no Pascal-side registry access, no named HKEY constant, no typed const, no hex literal, no char-literal concatenation. The [Code] section now uses only trivially-typed Inno primitives: Log, MsgBox, IsAdmin, DirExists, CreateDir, FileExists, ExpandConstant. r4 keeps the self-contained .NET 8 host + PFX/updater tools + docs + service registration + pre/post checks. Upstream v2.55.1 application tree + embedded Python are NOT in this payload (skipped network step on the dev build host); a full end-to-end build (with upstream source + Python 3.12 embeddable staged under {app}\app and {app}\python) requires running Build-Release.ps1 on a networked build host.
